**Finding: deviation (high severity, licence scope) — validated redline submitted.**

What I checked:
- **Grant clauses (§2.1–2.10)**: Commerce One grants to Corio; we are the licensee, so widening scope favours us.
- **Definitions (§1)**: "Corio Servers" ("owned or operated by or for Corio"), "Customers", "Software User" — no affiliate concept anywhere in the document (search for "Affiliate" returned zero hits).
- **§14.1 Assignment**, **§14.8 Subcontract**, **§11.2–11.3 Termination/survival**, **§14.9 Bankruptcy**.

Already compliant with the preferred position:
- §2.1 hosting licence is "perpetual and irrevocable"; §2.2 internal-use licence is "royalty-free, fully paid up, perpetual".
- §11.2 permits termination only for uncured 30-day material breach (plus insolvency), and §11.3 preserves our right to serve then-existing Customers post-termination.
- §14.1 permits assignment to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets without consent.

The gap:
- The grants run to **Corio alone**. Affiliates are never mentioned, and no grant names contractors — even though §14.8 expressly lets us subcontract portions of the Corio Services and the Corio Servers may be "operated by or for Corio". As drafted, an affiliate or subcontractor exercising the licensed rights sits outside the grant.

Redline (minimal, inserted as new §2.11 after §2.10): the Section 2 licences extend to Corio's affiliates and to contractors acting on Corio's behalf, limited to the Corio Services and our internal business operations, with Corio responsible for their compliance. Fallback offered in the comment: affiliate coverage on written notice.
